seed-cracker.message.started: Cracking the seed from the Nether %s at %s on %s threads. This takes up to a minute or so; you can keep playing.
seed-cracker.message.matches_all: It matches the bedrock in all %s Nether chunks read.
seed-cracker.message.matches_some: It matches the bedrock in %s of %s Nether chunks read. The rest were changed by players or generated before 1.18.
seed-cracker.message.unconfirmed: Not confirmed: the server's seed hash doesn't match any seed with these low 48 bits (structure seed %s), so the server may hide it. This is the seed if the world's seed was picked at random.
seed-cracker.message.structure_only: Only the low 48 bits are certain (the structure seed): that is enough for structures and most seed maps, not for biomes.
seed-cracker.message.retry: No seed fits that chunk's bedrock (players may have changed it). Trying another one.
seed-cracker.message.failed: Couldn't find the seed. The bedrock may have been changed, the Nether generated before 1.18, or the server isn't vanilla. Go somewhere else in the Nether and run /seedcracker start to try new chunks.
seed-cracker.message.error: Something went wrong (%s); see the game log.
seed-cracker.message.no_data: No Nether chunks read yet. Go to the Nether first.
seed-cracker.message.no_new_chunks: Every Nether chunk read so far has been tried. Go somewhere else in the Nether and run /seedcracker start again.
seed-cracker.message.check_match: Seed %s matches the Overworld bedrock: in %s of %s Overworld chunks read, every bedrock block in the floor is one this seed places. That depends on the whole seed; a wrong one gets some wrong in every chunk.
seed-cracker.message.check_mismatch: Seed %s doesn't match the Overworld bedrock: only %s of %s Overworld chunks read fit it. Either it's the wrong seed, or this Overworld isn't vanilla generation (superflat, custom world generation).
seed-cracker.message.check_no_data: No Overworld chunks read yet. Go to the Overworld (any loaded chunk will do) and run /seedcracker check again.
seed-cracker.message.check_no_seed: No seed to check yet. /seedcracker check <seed> checks any seed.
seed-cracker.status.chunks: Nether chunks read: %s (%s with an untouched floor, %s with an untouched roof)
seed-cracker.status.waiting: Not running. /seedcracker start cracks the seed from the Nether chunks read so far.
seed-cracker.status.failed: No seed found. /seedcracker start tries chunks it hasn't used yet.
seed-cracker.confidence.confirmed: confirmed by the server's seed hash
seed-cracker.confidence.random_seed_gues: not confirmed by the seed hash
seed-cracker.config.title: Seed Cracker
seed-cracker.config.commands_info: Go to the Nether and run /seedcracker start; it never starts by itself. /seedcracker stop stops it, /seedcracker shows what it's doing, /seedcracker check [seed] checks a seed against the Overworld bedrock. Seeds it finds are kept in config/seed-cracker-seeds.json, so a world is only cracked once.
seed-cracker.config.show_progress.toolti: Show how far along it is above the hotbar while it runs.
